result.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
result.comment: 43 pages, 10 figures, 21 tables, including Supplementary Information
result.summary: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, we can delete clinically defined waveform regions and alter beat timing to audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the clinically expected region was the strongest evidence in more than 90% of correct predictions. Bradycardia and tachycardia calls follow heart rate with conduction intervals held fixed, and atrial fibrillation calls vanish when beat-to-beat variation is removed. Sparse visibility graphs thus pair accurate ECG classification with clinically grounded, testable explanations.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LYNX-ECG，把每次心搏表示为带时间戳转折点的稀疏可见图并用 GNN 分类 ECG，同时通过删除临床定义的波形区域、改动心搏节律来审计预测依据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「节点对应具体时间点」的稀疏表示与按区域删除的因果审计，可供核查是否能迁移为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与贡献分配的评价手段，但论文本身不含多模态推理实验。
